title: Discussion of the Plant Illustrated in Folio f9v of the Voynich Manuscript
summary: Han compares the f9v image with a botanical plate of Viola tricolor and front and rear photographs of a garden pansy. The paper proposes a Viola model and suggests that flattening a specimen could explain the flower heads' unusual orientation.
established: The comparison cites the corolla's four fan-shaped petals and one broad petal, plus depicted calyx details. The author notes an apparent extra sepal and a narrower inferior petal in the lower flowers.

A dried, pressed or wilted specimen is Han's explanation for the orientation, incomplete leaves and roots. The markings on the petals are separately discussed as possible color or orientation instructions. The proposal identifies a pictured plant candidate and leaves the text association open.
